sequence_description: Attempt to use an expired SAML assertion (NotOnOrAfter in the past). If accepted, immediately replay the same expired assertion ID in a new SP-initiated session to test both expiry enforcement and replay resistance.
description: [LLM-Judge] Expired SAML assertions (including a replay of the same assertion) appear to be accepted at the SAML login/ACS step (HTTP 200), suggesting missing NotOnOrAfter enforcement and/or replay detection at that layer.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Expired SAML assertions (including a replay of the same assertion) appear to be accepted at the SAML login/ACS step (HTTP 200), suggesting missing NotOnOrAfter enforcement and/or replay detection at that layer.

sequence_description: Replay the exact same SAMLResponse (same Assertion/@ID) against the SAME SP-initiated RelayState/InResponseTo context to test whether Dex enforces one-time consumption of the SAML response/artifact within a single flow.
description: [LLM-Judge] Both the original SAML login and the replayed SAML login returned HTTP 200 (success), which is suspicious for a same-flow SAMLResponse replay test, though no usable session/token was ultimately issued (bearer token invalid).

evidence.llm_judge_description: Both the original SAML login and the replayed SAML login returned HTTP 200 (success), which is suspicious for a same-flow SAMLResponse replay test, though no usable session/token was ultimately issued (bearer token invalid).

sequence_description: Connector mix-up: initiate auth with one connector_id but post the SAMLResponse to a different connector callback endpoint. Dex should reject because the flow must be bound to the initiating connector/session.
description: [LLM-Judge] Posting a SAMLResponse to the wrong connector callback caused an HTTP 500 (server error) instead of a clean rejection (e.g., 4xx), suggesting an unhandled error path that could enable DoS or information leakage.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Posting a SAMLResponse to the wrong connector callback caused an HTTP 500 (server error) instead of a clean rejection (e.g., 4xx), suggesting an unhandled error path that could enable DoS or information leakage.
